stt: What's Up with Those Voices in Your Head?
x:
I'm not conflating them, they're already conflated and not
very well defined.

Consciousness implies "someone" that is conscious. A self-model in other words.

Babies, like most animals, do not possess consciousness in that sense, since in my view there is no self-model there to subjectively experience things.

A lot of us are simply assuming that there is but there is a lot
of anecdotal evidence that shows otherwise. Temporary self-model annihilation can be triggered in many ways and guess what happens? Bits of subjective experience (tastes, smells even pleasure and pain) disappear. People who have been through such experiences (ego-death) report in-hindsight that the feeling of being a conscious agent in space-time completely disappears, and it is simply as if one is absorbed into the environment, no longer separate from it.

In that way one can even view the myth of The Fall, as the emergence of consciousness, one is no longer one with nature but now separate from it.

Metziger's book is a good overview of such investigations:

https://www.amazon.com/Ego-Tunnel-Science-Mind-Myth/dp/04650...

x:
My personal favorite is Blindsight [0][1]. I read it multiple times (3 or 4, I think) over the years.

If you like Blindsight, you’ll probably want to continue with the sidequel, Echopraxia. You can also find them bundled together under the name Firefall.

And I think out of his main works, Blindsight is probably the most accessible. It also led me to Thomas Metzinger’s “The Ego Tunnel: The Science of the Mind and the Myth of the Self” [2], which Watts used as a source material in his research and had good things to say about.

The Rifters series is great, too, but there’s a sort of darkness or heaviness to it that may not work for everyone.

And bonus content, a fan made short movie based on Blindsight, here: [3].

I hope this helps. :)
